Bescon Consulting Engineers Pte
(BESCON)
is an
award winning
Professional Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) Engineering Consultancy and Project Management firm.
We provide a full range of
consulting services
including feasibility studies, conceptual & final design and construction management services.
Company Profile
Since its founding in 1972, our practice has grown to encompass a wide range of projects.
These range from residential, recreational, institutional, commercial and industrial to infrastructure projects
for clients both locally and regionally.
With a full complement of professional staff from the various engineering disciplines, clients can be
assured of the most comprehensive and highest standard of professional services.
Our overseas associates include P.T. Morimura and Associates of Japan
and
BES
Perunding
of Malaysia. This extensive pool of talent can be assembled into integrated
project teams to develop comprehensive and cost-effective approaches to
our clients� needs.
BESCON's
track record is proven and evident in the end result: building
services with innovative design solutions that meets and often exceeds clients� expectation for performance. The professionalism
of our service is evident in our dedication, conduct and undertaking of every project. It is through our personalised service
and attention that
BESCON
is the quality firm it is today.
Our Mission
Our mission is to add value to our clients' businesses by providing innovative,
quality and cost-effective expertise in Professional Engineering Consultancy Services. We are committed to performing our services
to the highest professional standard.
BESCON
aims to achieve excellence and meet our client's total satisfaction in
the provision of Professional Mechanical and Electrical Consultancy Services.
Our Philosophy
The continual exploration of Engineering ideas and skill to achieve the most
value added solution ranks high on our priority. We are constantly seeking out the latest technological advancement, paying
close attention to clients' requirements, aesthetics, functionality and economic elements of projects. We take the extra effort
to think from our clients' perspective - understanding their needs and tailoring our solutions to meet those needs.
Our commitment to this philosophy has resulted in many long-standing partnerships,
where

(BESCON)

for clients both locally and regionally.
With a full complement of professional staff from the various engineering disciplines, clients can be

and

Perunding

and attention that
BESCON

quality and cost-effective expertise in Professional Engineering Consultancy Services. We are committed to performing our services

Bescon Consulting Engineers Pte - About Us
Bescon Consulting Engineers Pte
(BESCON)
is an
award winning
Professional Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) Engineering Consultancy and Project Management firm.
We provide a full range of
consulting services
including feasibility studies, conceptual & final design and construction management services.
Company Profile
Since its founding in 1972, our practice has grown to encompass a wide range of projects.
These range from residential, recreational, institutional, commercial and industrial to infrastructure projects
for clients both locally and regionally.
With a full complement of professional staff from the various engineering disciplines, clients can be
assured of the most comprehensive and highest standard of professional services.
Our overseas associates include P.T. Morimura and Associates of Japan
and
BES
Perunding
of Malaysia. This extensive pool of talent can be assembled into integrated
project teams to develop comprehensive and cost-effective approaches to
our clients� needs.
BESCON's
track record is proven and evident in the end result: building
services with innovative design solutions that meets and often exceeds clients� expectation for performance. The professionalism
of our service is evident in our dedication, conduct and undertaking of every project. It is through our personalised service
and attention that
BESCON
is the quality firm it is today.
Our Mission
Our mission is to add value to our clients' businesses by providing innovative,
quality and cost-effective expertise in Professional Engineering Consultancy Services. We are committed to performing our services
to the highest professional standard.
BESCON
aims to achieve excellence and meet our client's total satisfaction in
the provision of Professional Mechanical and Electrical Consultancy Services.
Our Philosophy
The continual exploration of Engineering ideas and skill to achieve the most
value added solution ranks high on our priority. We are constantly seeking out the latest technological advancement, paying
close attention to clients' requirements, aesthetics, functionality and economic elements of projects. We take the extra effort
to think from our clients' perspective - understanding their needs and tailoring our solutions to meet those needs.
Our commitment to this philosophy has resulted in many long-standing partnerships,
where

Zeroqu founder & CEO featured in Ship Energy on 'second wave' of green retrofits
In
a recently published article in Ship Energy
Nitesh Ranvah
, our founder & CEO (who is also the group CEO at 21Knots Marine Engineering Consultancy) shared how a number of first movers and shipping giants having completed their first engine conversions and what this means is, a second wave of green retrofits is round the corner. It will be driven by owners of smaller fleets and can be expected in the next two to three years.
Nitesh and his team have recently worked with owners including two of the world largest container lines. They are now seeing a growing number of smaller shipowners entering the consultancy phase for green retrofit projects.
Two to three years will give these companies time to secure funding and align the retrofitting works with a planned dry dock.
"Once they have the roadmap, it's about creating the right financial setup to make those investments. They need to see when the vessels are going to dry dox, and they need to have the CAPEXâ
-Nitesh Ranvah

the full article here
for more on our vision for the future of green shipping, and how you can improve your ships.

Zero-Emission, Just-In-Time: Why Operational Synchronization is Maritime's Quickest Win
The future of shipping is vibrant, propelled by innovation in green fuels and pioneering propulsion systems. But what if the industry's most powerful, scalable, and immediate opportunity for massive emission cuts is already here?
It's time to celebrate the power of operational excellence and embrace a simple, smart solution that connects sea and shore for a cleaner future: Just-In-Time (JIT) Arrivals.
Turning Waste into Opportunity
For years, maritime operations followed a tough but inefficient rule: sail as fast as possible to secure your spot. This strategy, sadly, created a cycle of waste: vessels consumed excess fuel to rush, only to end up anchoring for hours or days, waiting for port logistics to catch up.
This isn't just a scheduling hiccup; itâs a huge missed opportunity for efficiency and sustainability, leading to avoidable costs, wasted time, and unnecessary CO2 emissions concentrated near our coastal communities.
Here's the stunning scale of that waste:
â¢
Financial Loss:
Industry reports estimate that port and anchorage delays can cost carriers anywhere from $15,000 to over $50,000 per day for large container vessels, amounting to billions of dollars annually across the sector.
â¢
Emission Cost:
A large container ship waiting at anchorage can still burn up to ~20 tonnes per day (depending on reefer load and vessel size). That is fuel wasted that could have been saved if the ship had sailed slower to arrive just-in-time.
â¢
Pollution Near Home:
The congestion near major ports means thousands of tonnes of extra NOx and particulate matter are released directly next to our coastal communities.
JIT: The Smartest Route to Zero
Just-In-Time arrival is the exciting next step in maritime evolution. It's a fundamental shift built on synchronization and intelligence.
By sharing real-time data on berth availability, cargo readiness, and port movements, ships can adjust their speed during the voyage. This allows them to operate at their optimal, most fuel-efficient engine load for the entire journey, ensuring they arrive exactly when the berth is ready.
This shift delivers immense, immediate environmental rewards:

Itâs about leveraging the digital tools we have and building stronger partnerships. It reframes decarbonization not just as a technology chase, but as a collective discipline based on trust and shared data.
Collaboration: Our Immediate Superpower
As the industry advances toward stricter global targets, JIT isn't just a good ideaâit's a testament to what we can achieve when we collaborate. It proves that by simply using data effectively, shipping can realize powerful emission reductions right now.
The future of shipping is punctual, efficient, and clean. Embracing JIT means seizing an immediate, scalable pathway toward lower emissions, making the movement of goods smarter and greener. Arriving precisely when needed is truly one of the most effective and positive steps the maritime industry can take today.
Decarbonization is not just about the technology we will have, but about optimizing the systems we do have.

The Great Race: Decoding the Fuels That Will Power Shipping's Future â½ï¸
Weâve all seen the headlines: Decarbonization is coming.
But what does that actually look like on the water? It means the comfortable, century-long reliance on heavy fuel oil is officially over. The maritime industry isn't just seeking a new energy source; it's entering a global, high-stakes competitionâa "Great Race"âto find the fuels that can power 90% of world trade, but without the carbon footprint.
The future of shipping is complex, messy, and exhilarating. Let's lift the hood on the contenders, from the liquid frontrunners to the vintage technologies making a stunning comeback.
The Heavyweight Contenders: Methanol & Ammonia
If you're asking which alternative fuels are winning the investment dollars right now, the answer lies in these two highly reactive liquids. They're the pragmatic choices, even with their flaws.
Methanol: The Safe Bet
Methanol is the industry's darling because it's the easiest to handle. Think of it as the friendly first step away from oil. Itâs liquid at ambient temperature, which means port terminals don't need a complete overhaul to start bunkering it. Yes, it still produces carbon when burned, but the path to
e-Methanol
(made using green hydrogen and captured COâ) offers a credible, carbon-neutral endpoint. Shipowners love it because itâs a tangible, near-term solution they can actually build for today.
Ammonia: The Zero-Carbon Game-Changer
Ammonia is the one that gets the engineers truly excited. It contains no carbon, so when used correctly, its combustion is truly zero-emission. Itâs also already a massive global commodity, so the infrastructure for transport exists, even if the marine fuel supply chain is nascent.
The Elephant in the Room:
Both require significant investment in new dual-fuel engines. More crucially, ammonia is toxic. Handling it demands entirely new safety regimes, vessel designs, and crew training. Itâs a high-risk, high-reward bet for the deep-sea routes of the 2030s and beyond.
The Vintage Comeback: Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) ð¬ï¸
Who says you need a complex chemical reaction to save the planet? Sometimes, the best innovation is dusting off a brilliant old idea.
Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) isn't about romantic sailing ships

[P014-C01] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
; itâs about modern, intelligent power augmentation. We're talking about massive, automated rotor sails (Flettner Rotors) or giant, computer-controlled wing sails that supplement the main engine.
Why are they back? Data.
Todayâs VPM systems allow operators to precisely calculate the optimal route to maximize wind conditions. This isnât guesswork; itâs a surgical application of power. WAP is a fantastic low-Capex solution that immediately cuts fuel consumption, drastically improves a vesselâs CII rating, and offers a straightforward, risk-free step toward decarbonization right now.
It proves that you don't always need an exotic fuel to make a massive environmental impact.
The Niche Players: Hydrogen & Electric Power ð
For all the talk of trans-oceanic voyages, the immediate adoption of green energy is happening closer to shore with electric and hydrogen solutions.
Hydrogen at Sea
Hydrogen is the cleanest flame, but it faces an insurmountable hurdle for large container ships: energy density. Simply put; to power a vessel across the Pacific, youâd need cryogenic hydrogen tanks so large they would swallow up most of your cargo space. It just doesn't make economic sense for the largest ships.
However, hydrogen is an ideal fit for short-sea and inland shipping. On routes where port calls are frequent and refuelling is easy, hydrogen fuel cells can generate electricity with zero emissions, creating green zones in harbours and coastal regions.
The Rise of Electric & Hybrid Vessels
Linked closely to hydrogen's niche are electric and hybrid vessels. These are dominating the ferry, tug, and coastal markets. By pairing efficient engines with large battery banks, these ships can switch to pure-electric mode when entering populated ports, eliminating local air pollution. The battery range limits their use, but for coastal trade where turnaround is quick, they are powerful, reliable, and fundamentally changing how local commerce operates.
Charting Your Course in a Multi-Fuel World
The message is clear: the future of maritime power isn't a simple fuel swap; it's a
multi-fuel ecosystem
Shipowners today are no longer just logistics experts; they are energy portfolio managers. The most successful fleets won't necessarily be the first to adopt the next fuel, but the ones that master the data to deploy the right fuel or technology for the right route at the right

[P014-C02] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
time.
This race is just beginning, and the strategy you adopt today will determine your fleet's profitability for the next thirty years.
Are you ready to navigate the change?

Foundations of Decarbonization: The Quest for Zero
The global shipping industry is sailing toward a radical transformation. For more than a century, we've relied on the cheap, reliable powerhouse of heavy fuel oil. But that chapter is closing.
The drive to achieve net-zero isn't just another environmental goal; it's a massive, non-negotiable business shift that is redefining fleet management, investment, and operational strategy. This "Quest for Zero" demands immediate action. Itâs about securing your profitability, managing catastrophic financial risks, and ensuring your vessels are built for the future, not the past. Let's unpack why this journey matters now and how to navigate the turbulent waters ahead.
Why the Quest for Zero is a Deadline, Not a Discussion ð¥
Weâre beyond soft guidelines. Today, three converging forces make decarbonization the most urgent item on your agenda:
The Regulator's Hammer (and the Carbon Tax):
New rules are landing with serious financial weight. The IMOâs CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) is actively grading your ships, and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is hitting you directly with a carbon price. If your vessel is inefficient, it earns a poor grade, and you pay a penalty. For some major routes, the cost of these carbon allowances is set to rival the cost of the fuel itself in the coming years. This is a direct tax on inefficiency.
The Capital Flow:
Money is getting picky. Investors, banks, and major financial institutions are pouring capital into ESG-compliant (Environmental, Social, and Governance) assets. If your fleet is dirty, financing gets more expensive, or simply disappears. Meanwhile, the world's biggest charterersâthe retailers, manufacturers, and commodity giantsâare demanding proof of green operations. If you canât deliver verifiable data, you lose the premium contracts.
The Hidden Profit Center:
Forget the CapEx for a minute. The fastest, easiest, and cheapest way to decarbonize is through operational efficiency. Implementing advanced Vessel Performance Management (VPM) allows you to squeeze every last drop of performance out of your existing assets. We're talking measurable savings from optimizing speed, recommending a better trim, or identifying hull fouling before it cos

The Big Picture: What IMOâs 2050 Targets Really Mean
The IMO's Revised GHG Strategy (2023) is the industry's compass. Its aggressive targets demand a complete overhaul:
The Destination:
Net-Zero by or around 2050. This is the big goal. It means that, globally, the industry must be carbon neutral. Logically, any deep-sea vessel built beyond the mid-2030s will have to be a true zero-emission ship to offset the legacy fleet.
The Crucial Milestones:
These require immediate attention: A 20% reduction in GHG emissions (from 2008 levels) by 2030. A 70% reduction in GHG emissions by 2040.
The Shipownerâs Takeaway:
The decade between 2030 and 2040 demands a 50% jump in emission cuts. Efficiency alone simply won't close that gap. This confirms that the fuel switch is non-negotiable. Any major asset investment todayâwhether it's a new build or a major retrofitâmust include a credible plan to transition to low-carbon fuels later in its life. If you're buying a ship today, it has to be profitable in the 70%-reduced world of 2040.

Zero-Emission, Just-In-Time: Why Operational Synchronization is Maritime's Quickest Win
The future of shipping is vibrant, propelled by innovation in green fuels and pioneering propulsion systems. But what if the industry's most powerful, scalable, and immediate opportunity for massive emission cuts is already here?
It's time to celebrate the power of operational excellence and embrace a simple, smart solution that connects sea and shore for a cleaner future: Just-In-Time (JIT) Arrivals.
Turning Waste into Opportunity
For years, maritime operations followed a tough but inefficient rule: sail as fast as possible to secure your spot. This strategy, sadly, created a cycle of waste: vessels consumed excess fuel to rush, only to end up anchoring for hours or days, waiting for port logistics to catch up.
This isn't just a scheduling hiccup; itâs a huge missed opportunity for efficiency and sustainability, leading to avoidable costs, wasted time, and unnecessary CO2 emissions concentrated near our coastal communities.
Here's the stunning scale of that waste:
â¢
Financial Loss:
Industry reports estimate that port and anchorage delays can cost carriers anywhere from $15,000 to over $50,000 per day for large container vessels, amounting to billions of dollars annually across the sector.
â¢
Emission Cost:
A large container ship waiting at anchorage can still burn up to ~20 tonnes per day (depending on reefer load and vessel size). That is fuel wasted that could have been saved if the ship had sailed slower to arrive just-in-time.
â¢
Pollution Near Home:
The congestion near major ports means thousands of tonnes of extra NOx and particulate matter are released directly next to our coastal communities.
JIT: The Smartest Route to Zero
Just-In-Time arrival is the exciting next step in maritime evolution. It's a fundamental shift built on synchronization and intelligence.
By sharing real-time data on berth availability, cargo readiness, and port movements, ships can adjust their speed during the voyage. This allows them to operate at their optimal, most fuel-efficient engine load for the entire journey, ensuring they arrive exactly when the berth is ready.
This shift delivers immense, immediate environmental rewards:

Traditional "Sail Fast, Wait Long"

The best news? JIT is a zero-emission enabler that requires no new hardware investment.
Itâs about leveraging the digital tools we have and building stronger partnerships. It reframes decarbonization not just as a technology chase, but as a collective discipline based on trust and shared data.
Collaboration: Our Immediate Superpower
As the industry advances toward stricter global targets, JIT isn't just a good ideaâit's a testament to what we can achieve when we collaborate. It proves that by simply using data effectively, shipping can realize powerful emission reductions right now.
The future of shipping is punctual, efficient, and clean. Embracing JIT means seizing an immediate, scalable pathway toward lower emissions, making the movement of goods smarter and greener. Arriving precisely when needed is truly one of the most effective and positive steps the maritime industry can take today.
Decarbonization is not just about the technology we will have, but about optimizing the systems we do have.

The Great Race: Decoding the Fuels That Will Power Shipping's Future â½ï¸
Weâve all seen the headlines: Decarbonization is coming.
But what does that actually look like on the water? It means the comfortable, century-long reliance on heavy fuel oil is officially over. The maritime industry isn't just seeking a new energy source; it's entering a global, high-stakes competitionâa "Great Race"âto find the fuels that can power 90% of world trade, but without the carbon footprint.
The future of shipping is complex, messy, and exhilarating. Let's lift the hood on the contenders, from the liquid frontrunners to the vintage technologies making a stunning comeback.
The Heavyweight Contenders: Methanol & Ammonia
If you're asking which alternative fuels are winning the investment dollars right now, the answer lies in these two highly reactive liquids. They're the pragmatic choices, even with their flaws.
Methanol: The Safe Bet
Methanol is the industry's darling because it's the easiest to handle. Think of it as the friendly first step away from oil. Itâs liquid at ambient temperature, which means port terminals don't need a complete overhaul to start bunkering it. Yes, it still produces carbon when burned, but the path to
e-Methanol
(made using green hydrogen and captured COâ) offers a credible, carbon-neutral endpoint. Shipowners love it because itâs a tangible, near-term solution they can actually build for today.
Ammonia: The Zero-Carbon Game-Changer
Ammonia is the one that gets the engineers truly excited. It contains no carbon, so when used correctly, its combustion is truly zero-emission. Itâs also already a massive global commodity, so the infrastructure for transport exists, even if the marine fuel supply chain is nascent.
The Elephant in the Room:
Both require significant investment in new dual-fuel engines. More crucially, ammonia is toxic. Handling it demands entirely new safety regimes, vessel designs, and crew training. Itâs a high-risk, high-reward bet for the deep-sea routes of the 2030s and beyond.
The Vintage Comeback: Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) ð¬ï¸
Who says you need a complex chemical reaction to save the planet? Sometimes, the best innovation is dusting off a brilliant old idea.
Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) isn't about romantic sailing ships

[P014-C01] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
; itâs about modern, intelligent power augmentation. We're talking about massive, automated rotor sails (Flettner Rotors) or giant, computer-controlled wing sails that supplement the main engine.
Why are they back? Data.
Todayâs VPM systems allow operators to precisely calculate the optimal route to maximize wind conditions. This isnât guesswork; itâs a surgical application of power. WAP is a fantastic low-Capex solution that immediately cuts fuel consumption, drastically improves a vesselâs CII rating, and offers a straightforward, risk-free step toward decarbonization right now.
It proves that you don't always need an exotic fuel to make a massive environmental impact.
The Niche Players: Hydrogen & Electric Power ð
For all the talk of trans-oceanic voyages, the immediate adoption of green energy is happening closer to shore with electric and hydrogen solutions.
Hydrogen at Sea
Hydrogen is the cleanest flame, but it faces an insurmountable hurdle for large container ships: energy density. Simply put; to power a vessel across the Pacific, youâd need cryogenic hydrogen tanks so large they would swallow up most of your cargo space. It just doesn't make economic sense for the largest ships.
However, hydrogen is an ideal fit for short-sea and inland shipping. On routes where port calls are frequent and refuelling is easy, hydrogen fuel cells can generate electricity with zero emissions, creating green zones in harbours and coastal regions.
The Rise of Electric & Hybrid Vessels
Linked closely to hydrogen's niche are electric and hybrid vessels. These are dominating the ferry, tug, and coastal markets. By pairing efficient engines with large battery banks, these ships can switch to pure-electric mode when entering populated ports, eliminating local air pollution. The battery range limits their use, but for coastal trade where turnaround is quick, they are powerful, reliable, and fundamentally changing how local commerce operates.
Charting Your Course in a Multi-Fuel World
The message is clear: the future of maritime power isn't a simple fuel swap; it's a
multi-fuel ecosystem
Shipowners today are no longer just logistics experts; they are energy portfolio managers. The most successful fleets won't necessarily be the first to adopt the next fuel, but the ones that master the data to deploy the right fuel or technology for the right route at the right

[P014-C02] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
time.
This race is just beginning, and the strategy you adopt today will determine your fleet's profitability for the next thirty years.
Are you ready to navigate the change?

Foundations of Decarbonization: The Quest for Zero
The global shipping industry is sailing toward a radical transformation. For more than a century, we've relied on the cheap, reliable powerhouse of heavy fuel oil. But that chapter is closing.
The drive to achieve net-zero isn't just another environmental goal; it's a massive, non-negotiable business shift that is redefining fleet management, investment, and operational strategy. This "Quest for Zero" demands immediate action. Itâs about securing your profitability, managing catastrophic financial risks, and ensuring your vessels are built for the future, not the past. Let's unpack why this journey matters now and how to navigate the turbulent waters ahead.
Why the Quest for Zero is a Deadline, Not a Discussion ð¥
Weâre beyond soft guidelines. Today, three converging forces make decarbonization the most urgent item on your agenda:
The Regulator's Hammer (and the Carbon Tax):
New rules are landing with serious financial weight. The IMOâs CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) is actively grading your ships, and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is hitting you directly with a carbon price. If your vessel is inefficient, it earns a poor grade, and you pay a penalty. For some major routes, the cost of these carbon allowances is set to rival the cost of the fuel itself in the coming years. This is a direct tax on inefficiency.
The Capital Flow:
Money is getting picky. Investors, banks, and major financial institutions are pouring capital into ESG-compliant (Environmental, Social, and Governance) assets. If your fleet is dirty, financing gets more expensive, or simply disappears. Meanwhile, the world's biggest charterersâthe retailers, manufacturers, and commodity giantsâare demanding proof of green operations. If you canât deliver verifiable data, you lose the premium contracts.
The Hidden Profit Center:
Forget the CapEx for a minute. The fastest, easiest, and cheapest way to decarbonize is through operational efficiency. Implementing advanced Vessel Performance Management (VPM) allows you to squeeze every last drop of performance out of your existing assets. We're talking measurable savings from optimizing speed, recommending a better trim, or identifying hull fouling before it cos

ts you thousands in unnecessary fuel burn. It's instant OPEX reduction that also cuts your carbon footprint.
The Big Picture: What IMOâs 2050 Targets Really Mean
The IMO's Revised GHG Strategy (2023) is the industry's compass. Its aggressive targets demand a complete overhaul:
The Destination:
Net-Zero by or around 2050. This is the big goal. It means that, globally, the industry must be carbon neutral. Logically, any deep-sea vessel built beyond the mid-2030s will have to be a true zero-emission ship to offset the legacy fleet.
The Crucial Milestones:
These require immediate attention: A 20% reduction in GHG emissions (from 2008 levels) by 2030. A 70% reduction in GHG emissions by 2040.
The Shipownerâs Takeaway:
The decade between 2030 and 2040 demands a 50% jump in emission cuts. Efficiency alone simply won't close that gap. This confirms that the fuel switch is non-negotiable. Any major asset investment todayâwhether it's a new build or a major retrofitâmust include a credible plan to transition to low-carbon fuels later in its life. If you're buying a ship today, it has to be profitable in the 70%-reduced world of 2040.

Zero-Emission, Just-In-Time: Why Operational Synchronization is Maritime's Quickest Win
The future of shipping is vibrant, propelled by innovation in green fuels and pioneering propulsion systems. But what if the industry's most powerful, scalable, and immediate opportunity for massive emission cuts is already here?
It's time to celebrate the power of operational excellence and embrace a simple, smart solution that connects sea and shore for a cleaner future: Just-In-Time (JIT) Arrivals.
Turning Waste into Opportunity
For years, maritime operations followed a tough but inefficient rule: sail as fast as possible to secure your spot. This strategy, sadly, created a cycle of waste: vessels consumed excess fuel to rush, only to end up anchoring for hours or days, waiting for port logistics to catch up.
This isn't just a scheduling hiccup; itâs a huge missed opportunity for efficiency and sustainability, leading to avoidable costs, wasted time, and unnecessary CO2 emissions concentrated near our coastal communities.
Here's the stunning scale of that waste:
â¢
Financial Loss:
Industry reports estimate that port and anchorage delays can cost carriers anywhere from $15,000 to over $50,000 per day for large container vessels, amounting to billions of dollars annually across the sector.
â¢
Emission Cost:
A large container ship waiting at anchorage can still burn up to ~20 tonnes per day (depending on reefer load and vessel size). That is fuel wasted that could have been saved if the ship had sailed slower to arrive just-in-time.
â¢
Pollution Near Home:
The congestion near major ports means thousands of tonnes of extra NOx and particulate matter are released directly next to our coastal communities.
JIT: The Smartest Route to Zero
Just-In-Time arrival is the exciting next step in maritime evolution. It's a fundamental shift built on synchronization and intelligence.
By sharing real-time data on berth availability, cargo readiness, and port movements, ships can adjust their speed during the voyage. This allows them to operate at their optimal, most fuel-efficient engine load for the entire journey, ensuring they arrive exactly when the berth is ready.
This shift delivers immense, immediate environmental rewards:
Feature
Traditional "Sail Fast, Wait Long"

The best news? JIT is a zero-emission enabler that requires no new hardware investment.
Itâs about leveraging the digital tools we have and building stronger partnerships. It reframes decarbonization not just as a technology chase, but as a collective discipline based on trust and shared data.
Collaboration: Our Immediate Superpower
As the industry advances toward stricter global targets, JIT isn't just a good ideaâit's a testament to what we can achieve when we collaborate. It proves that by simply using data effectively, shipping can realize powerful emission reductions right now.
The future of shipping is punctual, efficient, and clean. Embracing JIT means seizing an immediate, scalable pathway toward lower emissions, making the movement of goods smarter and greener. Arriving precisely when needed is truly one of the most effective and positive steps the maritime industry can take today.
Decarbonization is not just about the technology we will have, but about optimizing the systems we do have.

The Great Race: Decoding the Fuels That Will Power Shipping's Future â½ï¸
Weâve all seen the headlines: Decarbonization is coming.
But what does that actually look like on the water? It means the comfortable, century-long reliance on heavy fuel oil is officially over. The maritime industry isn't just seeking a new energy source; it's entering a global, high-stakes competitionâa "Great Race"âto find the fuels that can power 90% of world trade, but without the carbon footprint.
The future of shipping is complex, messy, and exhilarating. Let's lift the hood on the contenders, from the liquid frontrunners to the vintage technologies making a stunning comeback.
The Heavyweight Contenders: Methanol & Ammonia
If you're asking which alternative fuels are winning the investment dollars right now, the answer lies in these two highly reactive liquids. They're the pragmatic choices, even with their flaws.
Methanol: The Safe Bet
Methanol is the industry's darling because it's the easiest to handle. Think of it as the friendly first step away from oil. Itâs liquid at ambient temperature, which means port terminals don't need a complete overhaul to start bunkering it. Yes, it still produces carbon when burned, but the path to
e-Methanol
(made using green hydrogen and captured COâ) offers a credible, carbon-neutral endpoint. Shipowners love it because itâs a tangible, near-term solution they can actually build for today.
Ammonia: The Zero-Carbon Game-Changer
Ammonia is the one that gets the engineers truly excited. It contains no carbon, so when used correctly, its combustion is truly zero-emission. Itâs also already a massive global commodity, so the infrastructure for transport exists, even if the marine fuel supply chain is nascent.
The Elephant in the Room:
Both require significant investment in new dual-fuel engines. More crucially, ammonia is toxic. Handling it demands entirely new safety regimes, vessel designs, and crew training. Itâs a high-risk, high-reward bet for the deep-sea routes of the 2030s and beyond.
The Vintage Comeback: Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) ð¬ï¸
Who says you need a complex chemical reaction to save the planet? Sometimes, the best innovation is dusting off a brilliant old idea.
Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) isn't about romantic sailing ships

[P014-C01] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
; itâs about modern, intelligent power augmentation. We're talking about massive, automated rotor sails (Flettner Rotors) or giant, computer-controlled wing sails that supplement the main engine.
Why are they back? Data.
Todayâs VPM systems allow operators to precisely calculate the optimal route to maximize wind conditions. This isnât guesswork; itâs a surgical application of power. WAP is a fantastic low-Capex solution that immediately cuts fuel consumption, drastically improves a vesselâs CII rating, and offers a straightforward, risk-free step toward decarbonization right now.
It proves that you don't always need an exotic fuel to make a massive environmental impact.
The Niche Players: Hydrogen & Electric Power ð
For all the talk of trans-oceanic voyages, the immediate adoption of green energy is happening closer to shore with electric and hydrogen solutions.
Hydrogen at Sea
Hydrogen is the cleanest flame, but it faces an insurmountable hurdle for large container ships: energy density. Simply put; to power a vessel across the Pacific, youâd need cryogenic hydrogen tanks so large they would swallow up most of your cargo space. It just doesn't make economic sense for the largest ships.
However, hydrogen is an ideal fit for short-sea and inland shipping. On routes where port calls are frequent and refuelling is easy, hydrogen fuel cells can generate electricity with zero emissions, creating green zones in harbours and coastal regions.
The Rise of Electric & Hybrid Vessels
Linked closely to hydrogen's niche are electric and hybrid vessels. These are dominating the ferry, tug, and coastal markets. By pairing efficient engines with large battery banks, these ships can switch to pure-electric mode when entering populated ports, eliminating local air pollution. The battery range limits their use, but for coastal trade where turnaround is quick, they are powerful, reliable, and fundamentally changing how local commerce operates.
Charting Your Course in a Multi-Fuel World
The message is clear: the future of maritime power isn't a simple fuel swap; it's a
multi-fuel ecosystem
Shipowners today are no longer just logistics experts; they are energy portfolio managers. The most successful fleets won't necessarily be the first to adopt the next fuel, but the ones that master the data to deploy the right fuel or technology for the right route at the right

[P014-C02] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
time.
This race is just beginning, and the strategy you adopt today will determine your fleet's profitability for the next thirty years.
Are you ready to navigate the change?

Foundations of Decarbonization: The Quest for Zero
The global shipping industry is sailing toward a radical transformation. For more than a century, we've relied on the cheap, reliable powerhouse of heavy fuel oil. But that chapter is closing.
The drive to achieve net-zero isn't just another environmental goal; it's a massive, non-negotiable business shift that is redefining fleet management, investment, and operational strategy. This "Quest for Zero" demands immediate action. Itâs about securing your profitability, managing catastrophic financial risks, and ensuring your vessels are built for the future, not the past. Let's unpack why this journey matters now and how to navigate the turbulent waters ahead.
Why the Quest for Zero is a Deadline, Not a Discussion ð¥
Weâre beyond soft guidelines. Today, three converging forces make decarbonization the most urgent item on your agenda:
The Regulator's Hammer (and the Carbon Tax):
New rules are landing with serious financial weight. The IMOâs CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) is actively grading your ships, and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is hitting you directly with a carbon price. If your vessel is inefficient, it earns a poor grade, and you pay a penalty. For some major routes, the cost of these carbon allowances is set to rival the cost of the fuel itself in the coming years. This is a direct tax on inefficiency.
The Capital Flow:
Money is getting picky. Investors, banks, and major financial institutions are pouring capital into ESG-compliant (Environmental, Social, and Governance) assets. If your fleet is dirty, financing gets more expensive, or simply disappears. Meanwhile, the world's biggest charterersâthe retailers, manufacturers, and commodity giantsâare demanding proof of green operations. If you canât deliver verifiable data, you lose the premium contracts.
The Hidden Profit Center:
Forget the CapEx for a minute. The fastest, easiest, and cheapest way to decarbonize is through operational efficiency. Implementing advanced Vessel Performance Management (VPM) allows you to squeeze every last drop of performance out of your existing assets. We're talking measurable savings from optimizing speed, recommending a better trim, or identifying hull fouling before it cos

ts you thousands in unnecessary fuel burn. It's instant OPEX reduction that also cuts your carbon footprint.
The Big Picture: What IMOâs 2050 Targets Really Mean
The IMO's Revised GHG Strategy (2023) is the industry's compass. Its aggressive targets demand a complete overhaul:
The Destination:
Net-Zero by or around 2050. This is the big goal. It means that, globally, the industry must be carbon neutral. Logically, any deep-sea vessel built beyond the mid-2030s will have to be a true zero-emission ship to offset the legacy fleet.
The Crucial Milestones:
These require immediate attention: A 20% reduction in GHG emissions (from 2008 levels) by 2030. A 70% reduction in GHG emissions by 2040.
The Shipownerâs Takeaway:
The decade between 2030 and 2040 demands a 50% jump in emission cuts. Efficiency alone simply won't close that gap. This confirms that the fuel switch is non-negotiable. Any major asset investment todayâwhether it's a new build or a major retrofitâmust include a credible plan to transition to low-carbon fuels later in its life. If you're buying a ship today, it has to be profitable in the 70%-reduced world of 2040.

Zero-Emission, Just-In-Time: Why Operational Synchronization is Maritime's Quickest Win
The future of shipping is vibrant, propelled by innovation in green fuels and pioneering propulsion systems. But what if the industry's most powerful, scalable, and immediate opportunity for massive emission cuts is already here?
It's time to celebrate the power of operational excellence and embrace a simple, smart solution that connects sea and shore for a cleaner future: Just-In-Time (JIT) Arrivals.
Turning Waste into Opportunity
For years, maritime operations followed a tough but inefficient rule: sail as fast as possible to secure your spot. This strategy, sadly, created a cycle of waste: vessels consumed excess fuel to rush, only to end up anchoring for hours or days, waiting for port logistics to catch up.
This isn't just a scheduling hiccup; itâs a huge missed opportunity for efficiency and sustainability, leading to avoidable costs, wasted time, and unnecessary CO2 emissions concentrated near our coastal communities.
Here's the stunning scale of that waste:
â¢
Financial Loss:
Industry reports estimate that port and anchorage delays can cost carriers anywhere from $15,000 to over $50,000 per day for large container vessels, amounting to billions of dollars annually across the sector.
â¢
Emission Cost:
A large container ship waiting at anchorage can still burn up to ~20 tonnes per day (depending on reefer load and vessel size). That is fuel wasted that could have been saved if the ship had sailed slower to arrive just-in-time.
â¢
Pollution Near Home:
The congestion near major ports means thousands of tonnes of extra NOx and particulate matter are released directly next to our coastal communities.
JIT: The Smartest Route to Zero
Just-In-Time arrival is the exciting next step in maritime evolution. It's a fundamental shift built on synchronization and intelligence.
By sharing real-time data on berth availability, cargo readiness, and port movements, ships can adjust their speed during the voyage. This allows them to operate at their optimal, most fuel-efficient engine load for the entire journey, ensuring they arrive exactly when the berth is ready.
This shift delivers immense, immediate environmental rewards:

The best news? JIT is a zero-emission enabler that requires no new hardware investment.
Itâs about leveraging the digital tools we have and building stronger partnerships. It reframes decarbonization not just as a technology chase, but as a collective discipline based on trust and shared data.
Collaboration: Our Immediate Superpower
As the industry advances toward stricter global targets, JIT isn't just a good ideaâit's a testament to what we can achieve when we collaborate. It proves that by simply using data effectively, shipping can realize powerful emission reductions right now.
The future of shipping is punctual, efficient, and clean. Embracing JIT means seizing an immediate, scalable pathway toward lower emissions, making the movement of goods smarter and greener. Arriving precisely when needed is truly one of the most effective and positive steps the maritime industry can take today.
Decarbonization is not just about the technology we will have, but about optimizing the systems we do have.

The Great Race: Decoding the Fuels That Will Power Shipping's Future â½ï¸
Weâve all seen the headlines: Decarbonization is coming.
But what does that actually look like on the water? It means the comfortable, century-long reliance on heavy fuel oil is officially over. The maritime industry isn't just seeking a new energy source; it's entering a global, high-stakes competitionâa "Great Race"âto find the fuels that can power 90% of world trade, but without the carbon footprint.
The future of shipping is complex, messy, and exhilarating. Let's lift the hood on the contenders, from the liquid frontrunners to the vintage technologies making a stunning comeback.
The Heavyweight Contenders: Methanol & Ammonia
If you're asking which alternative fuels are winning the investment dollars right now, the answer lies in these two highly reactive liquids. They're the pragmatic choices, even with their flaws.
Methanol: The Safe Bet
Methanol is the industry's darling because it's the easiest to handle. Think of it as the friendly first step away from oil. Itâs liquid at ambient temperature, which means port terminals don't need a complete overhaul to start bunkering it. Yes, it still produces carbon when burned, but the path to
e-Methanol
(made using green hydrogen and captured COâ) offers a credible, carbon-neutral endpoint. Shipowners love it because itâs a tangible, near-term solution they can actually build for today.
Ammonia: The Zero-Carbon Game-Changer
Ammonia is the one that gets the engineers truly excited. It contains no carbon, so when used correctly, its combustion is truly zero-emission. Itâs also already a massive global commodity, so the infrastructure for transport exists, even if the marine fuel supply chain is nascent.
The Elephant in the Room:
Both require significant investment in new dual-fuel engines. More crucially, ammonia is toxic. Handling it demands entirely new safety regimes, vessel designs, and crew training. Itâs a high-risk, high-reward bet for the deep-sea routes of the 2030s and beyond.
The Vintage Comeback: Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) ð¬ï¸
Who says you need a complex chemical reaction to save the planet? Sometimes, the best innovation is dusting off a brilliant old idea.
Wind-Assisted Propulsion (WAP) isn't about romantic sailing ships

[P014-C01] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
; itâs about modern, intelligent power augmentation. We're talking about massive, automated rotor sails (Flettner Rotors) or giant, computer-controlled wing sails that supplement the main engine.
Why are they back? Data.
Todayâs VPM systems allow operators to precisely calculate the optimal route to maximize wind conditions. This isnât guesswork; itâs a surgical application of power. WAP is a fantastic low-Capex solution that immediately cuts fuel consumption, drastically improves a vesselâs CII rating, and offers a straightforward, risk-free step toward decarbonization right now.
It proves that you don't always need an exotic fuel to make a massive environmental impact.
The Niche Players: Hydrogen & Electric Power ð
For all the talk of trans-oceanic voyages, the immediate adoption of green energy is happening closer to shore with electric and hydrogen solutions.
Hydrogen at Sea
Hydrogen is the cleanest flame, but it faces an insurmountable hurdle for large container ships: energy density. Simply put; to power a vessel across the Pacific, youâd need cryogenic hydrogen tanks so large they would swallow up most of your cargo space. It just doesn't make economic sense for the largest ships.
However, hydrogen is an ideal fit for short-sea and inland shipping. On routes where port calls are frequent and refuelling is easy, hydrogen fuel cells can generate electricity with zero emissions, creating green zones in harbours and coastal regions.
The Rise of Electric & Hybrid Vessels
Linked closely to hydrogen's niche are electric and hybrid vessels. These are dominating the ferry, tug, and coastal markets. By pairing efficient engines with large battery banks, these ships can switch to pure-electric mode when entering populated ports, eliminating local air pollution. The battery range limits their use, but for coastal trade where turnaround is quick, they are powerful, reliable, and fundamentally changing how local commerce operates.
Charting Your Course in a Multi-Fuel World
The message is clear: the future of maritime power isn't a simple fuel swap; it's a
multi-fuel ecosystem
Shipowners today are no longer just logistics experts; they are energy portfolio managers. The most successful fleets won't necessarily be the first to adopt the next fuel, but the ones that master the data to deploy the right fuel or technology for the right route at the right

[P014-C02] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-great-race-decoding-the-fuels-that-will-power-shippings-future
time.
This race is just beginning, and the strategy you adopt today will determine your fleet's profitability for the next thirty years.
Are you ready to navigate the change?

Foundations of Decarbonization: The Quest for Zero
The global shipping industry is sailing toward a radical transformation. For more than a century, we've relied on the cheap, reliable powerhouse of heavy fuel oil. But that chapter is closing.
The drive to achieve net-zero isn't just another environmental goal; it's a massive, non-negotiable business shift that is redefining fleet management, investment, and operational strategy. This "Quest for Zero" demands immediate action. Itâs about securing your profitability, managing catastrophic financial risks, and ensuring your vessels are built for the future, not the past. Let's unpack why this journey matters now and how to navigate the turbulent waters ahead.
Why the Quest for Zero is a Deadline, Not a Discussion ð¥
Weâre beyond soft guidelines. Today, three converging forces make decarbonization the most urgent item on your agenda:
The Regulator's Hammer (and the Carbon Tax):
New rules are landing with serious financial weight. The IMOâs CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) is actively grading your ships, and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is hitting you directly with a carbon price. If your vessel is inefficient, it earns a poor grade, and you pay a penalty. For some major routes, the cost of these carbon allowances is set to rival the cost of the fuel itself in the coming years. This is a direct tax on inefficiency.
The Capital Flow:
Money is getting picky. Investors, banks, and major financial institutions are pouring capital into ESG-compliant (Environmental, Social, and Governance) assets. If your fleet is dirty, financing gets more expensive, or simply disappears. Meanwhile, the world's biggest charterersâthe retailers, manufacturers, and commodity giantsâare demanding proof of green operations. If you canât deliver verifiable data, you lose the premium contracts.
The Hidden Profit Center:
Forget the CapEx for a minute. The fastest, easiest, and cheapest way to decarbonize is through operational efficiency. Implementing advanced Vessel Performance Management (VPM) allows you to squeeze every last drop of performance out of your existing assets. We're talking measurable savings from optimizing speed, recommending a better trim, or identifying hull fouling before it cos

[P015-C01] https://www.zeroqu.com/news-articles/the-quest-for-zero-foundations-of-decarbonization-why-the-quest-for-zero-is-a-deadline-not-a-discussion-c9doz
ts you thousands in unnecessary fuel burn. It's instant OPEX reduction that also cuts your carbon footprint.
The Big Picture: What IMOâs 2050 Targets Really Mean
The IMO's Revised GHG Strategy (2023) is the industry's compass. Its aggressive targets demand a complete overhaul:
The Destination:
Net-Zero by or around 2050. This is the big goal. It means that, globally, the industry must be carbon neutral. Logically, any deep-sea vessel built beyond the mid-2030s will have to be a true zero-emission ship to offset the legacy fleet.
The Crucial Milestones:
These require immediate attention: A 20% reduction in GHG emissions (from 2008 levels) by 2030. A 70% reduction in GHG emissions by 2040.
The Shipownerâs Takeaway:
The decade between 2030 and 2040 demands a 50% jump in emission cuts. Efficiency alone simply won't close that gap. This confirms that the fuel switch is non-negotiable. Any major asset investment todayâwhether it's a new build or a major retrofitâmust include a credible plan to transition to low-carbon fuels later in its life. If you're buying a ship today, it has to be profitable in the 70%-reduced world of 2040.
Fuel Option
The Selling Point
The Reality Check
Drop-in Biofuels
Fastest Win: Compatible with existing engines for immediate cuts.
Limited Supply: High cost and constrained global supply. A good short-term fix, not a long-term solution.
Methanol (CHâOH)
Current Frontrunner: Liquid at ambient temperatures, easier to handle than others.
Lower Energy Density: Requires larger storage tanks. A leading choice for the current wave of dual-fuel new builds.
Ammonia (NHâ)
The Deep-Sea Hope: A powerful zero-carbon carrier for long-haul routes.
Toxicity is Key: Requires intensive safety protocols and advanced engine technology still being scaled up. A massive long-term investment.
Hydrogen (Hâ)
True Zero: Zero emissions at the point of combustion.
Logistical Nightmare: Extremely low density requires huge, cryogenic storage. Best suited for short-sea, ferry, and harbour vessels.
The smartest move you can make today is ensuring "future-fuel readiness." Investing a little extra now to make your new vessels compatible with future fuelsâwhether that's methanol or ammoniaâbuys you the flexibility to adapt later without stranding billions in capital. The transition is challenging, but clarity is power. Optimize your current operations with

data, and strategically plan for fuel flexibility to master the inevitable voyage to net-zero.
